raw_response:
Alright, let me think through this year's plan. I've been working this 7.5 mu for a long time, and vegetables are what pays the bills around here. Grain won't feed a family of three with decent clothes — you need cash crops.

My cabbage-chili rotation is the main thing. Cabbage goes in early spring, I pull it in late May or early June, then the chili transplants go in right after on the same ground. Eggplant and kidney bean are on separate small plots, and I keep one mu of summer maize mostly for the household and for feeding chickens — not really for selling.

The extension guy came around last winter and talked about balanced fertilizer, but honestly I mostly do what worked last year. For the vegetables I always put down chicken manure first — I get it cheap from the layer farm in the next village, about 2 cubic meters per mu — then compound fertilizer. Vegetables eat a lot, you can't be stingy or the heads won't fill out and the chili plants stay small.

Water isn't too much of a problem because I have the tube well, but pumping costs electricity. I irrigate cabbage more in April when the heads are forming, and chili gets water whenever it looks thirsty in July-August heat.

Pests are the big worry. Cabbage worms every year, and the chili gets aphids and sometimes blight. I spray when I see them, not on a schedule — spraying costs money and my wife worries about the chemicals.

Labor — it's me, my wife, and my son when he's not working at the factory in town. Three of us can handle 7.5 mu of vegetables if we plan the picking right, but for transplanting and big harvest days I sometimes pay a neighbor 80-100 yuan a day.
